card.name: Verbs and quantifiers after a subject
card.fires_on: Short function words in general web prose, mostly a verb like were, have or will right after a plural subject, or any and aspect after a noun phrase. Seen mostly in news or interview text.

modes.label: Verb after subject
modes.description: Auxiliary or plural verb (were, have, will) following a subject or a dash aside.
modes.example: Aburto-Oropeza says the changes<< have>> occurred at the hands of fishing activities.

modes.label: The word aspect
modes.description: The noun aspect after most rewarding or one.
modes.example: Laura: The most rewarding<< aspect>> of your job?

modes.label: The word any
modes.description: Any used before idea or indication.
modes.example: if this album cover is<< any>> indication, he is white.

card.plain: It fires on small connecting words in ordinary news prose, such as were, have, any and aspect.
evidence: Laura: The most rewarding<< aspect>> of your job?
Aburto-Oropeza says the changes<< have>> occurred at the hands of fishing activities.
if this album cover is<< any>> indication, he is white.
